preconditions.description: The input binary string s has length at most 2000.

preconditions.expression: all(c in '01' for c in s)
preconditions.description: The input string s consists only of characters '0' and '1'.
The input string s is non-empty.

postconditions.description: The output string t has the same length as the input string s.

postconditions.expression: all(c in '01' for c in t)
postconditions.description: The output string t consists only of characters '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: all(longest_non_decreasing_subseq_len(s[l:r+1]) == longest_non_decreasing_subseq_len(t[l:r+1]) for l in range(len(s)) for r in range(l, len(s)))
postconditions.description: For every substring defined by indices l and r (1-based in problem, 0-based here), the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence in s[l:r+1] equals that in t[l:r+1].

postconditions.expression: t.count('0') == max(cand.count('0') for cand in all_valid_candidates(s))
postconditions.description: The number of zeroes in t is the maximum possible among all binary strings of length n that satisfy the subsequence length condition for all substrings.
